deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a working outline, a table of contents with drafts of opening sentences, for Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Ueber die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1853–54, published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). The previous page (199r) is consistent with this. It discusses Dirichlet's 1829 Crelle paper: Dirichlet assumes a finite, piecewise continuous function, his reasoning extends to some cases of infinitely many oscillations, and a later note treats functions that become infinite.

Structure visible on 199v, compared with the published paper:

(a) First attempt at §1. 'd'Alembert, Euler, Daniel Bernoulli', with 'Euler' rewritten and 'Daniel' added above. A draft sentence follows: 'Die Frage über die Darstellbarkeit einer willkürlichen Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe entsteht bei den Untersuchungen über die schwingenden [Saiten]'. A partly struck heading follows, very probably 'Von Euler bis Fourier'. This is exactly the title of §1 of the published paper.

(b) Revised plan. §1 is Fourier's work (first word uncertain). §2 is 'Von Fourier bis Dirichlet'. §3 is 'Seit Dirichlet', struck and rewritten; a struck variant reads 'Was Dirichlet ... übrig [ließ]'. Next comes 'Über den Begriff eines bestimmten Integrals und den Umfang seiner Gültigkeit'. That is verbatim the title of the published §4. Below it is '§4. Definition des Begriffs', which became the Riemann integral definition in the paper. A sentence begins 'Die Frage über die Dar[stellbarkeit]'.

(c) The final draft of the opening sentence of §1: 'Ursprung der Frage aus dem Streit über die Tragweite der d'Alembert'schen und der Bernoulli'schen Lösung des Problems der schwingenden Saiten im Jahre 1753.' The published §1 indeed begins with the 1753 controversy:
- d'Alembert's general solution y = f(x+t) + g(x−t) of y_tt = y_xx (1747);
- Euler's arbitrary initial shapes;
- Daniel Bernoulli's 1753 claim that every motion is a superposition sum a_n sin(n x) cos(n t + phi_n).

Non-mathematical items:
- 'cav. Stern' at top right, probably a note concerning M. A. Stern, the Göttingen professor.
- 'Herbart: Allgemeine Metaphysik', a reading note reflecting Riemann's known study of Herbart.
- 'A. Ritter stud. math. / Weender Str. Müller' in a different hand or ink: a student's name and lodging address, unrelated to the text.
- A red archival or reference mark 'Rm 3. § 3.'
- At the right, a vertical column of numbers (24,24; 57,14; 58,26; 58,22; 58,08). These look like measurement readings, perhaps degrees and minutes or minutes and seconds. They possibly relate to the physics notes nearby (the next page has 'Nobilische Farbenringe'). Their purpose cannot be determined, and they are not derivations.

No computation is performed on the page.
errors: None mathematical. The historical claim (dispute over d'Alembert's vs. Bernoulli's solution of the vibrating string in 1753) is accurate: D. Bernoulli's memoir is from 1753 and appeared in the Berlin Mémoires for 1753 (published 1755).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft outline whose headings and opening sentence match the published Habilitationsschrift almost verbatim. It is of minor interest for the genesis of the text, for example the earlier ordering and the struck 'Was Dirichlet übrig ließ'. It contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: d'Alembert's general solution satisfies the wave equation y_tt = y_xx (unit speed).
Each of Bernoulli's standing-wave modes satisfies the wave equation and vanishes at x=0 and x=pi.
Each Bernoulli mode is of d'Alembert form, the identity underlying the 1753 dispute.

transcription_corrections: The struck line read as '[-Nach[?] Begriff[?] ... Euler bei Fourier.-]' is most likely 'Von Euler bis Fourier', the published §1 title.
'§. 2. [-?-] Fourier und Dirichlet' is likely 'Von Fourier bis Dirichlet', the published §2 title.
The struck '§. 3. Seit[?] Dirichlet' is consistent with 'Seit Dirichlet', the published §3 title; the following struck line probably reads 'Was Dirichlet ... übrig [ließ]'.
'd. eine trigonometrische Reihe' should be expanded to 'durch eine trigonometrische Reihe'; the struck ending is 'bei den Untersuchungen über die schwingenden [Saiten]'.
'{+Daniel+}' is added above 'Bernoulli' in the §1 heading, so it reads 'Daniel Bernoulli'.
'cav. Stern' is uncertain; it is possibly 'cand.' or another abbreviation before Stern (M. A. Stern).
'A. Ritter stud. math. / Weender Str. Müller' is in a different ink and hand: an address note, not part of the text.
The first word of the second '§. 1.' line ('Beiträge[?]') is uncertain; it may be 'Kritische' or similar, followed by 'Arbeit Fourier's'.
